doc.title: Konitz Lee — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: The Giuffre saxophone section album
summary: Konitz says Giuffre created the album; he picked Marsh and Brown, and not the rhythm section.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: The next record is a few months later in May of fifty-nine. Lee Konitz Meets Jimmy Giuffre and the Saxophone Section.
Yeah that was a nice one.
I think Norman Granz had some suggestion about that. That’s all I really know about that. Jimmy suggested it and created it basically.
Did you decide who was going to be in the section? Because it’s Hal McKusick, Warne, Ted Brown, and Jimmy Giuffre. Were those your choices?
I would think Warne and Ted would’ve been. I didn’t know Hal that well but its possible. I would say Hal was probably suggested by Jimmy. I had nothing to say about the rhythm section I remember.
The rhythm section, by the way, is Bill Evans, Buddy Clark, and the now legendary Ronnie Free.
That’s one of the few records he’s on.
Yeah. Someone just gave me regards from him.
